summary: The application demonstrates a strong, modern foundation with a clean aesthetic heavily influenced by Vercel and Linear. To reach top-tier industry grade, it needs refinement in typography scaling (reducing oversized headers), reduction of always-visible actions in list views to reduce clutter, and modernization of card visuals to maintain a consistent 'dense-but-calm' feel.

typography.note: Generally clean sans-serif, but some headers (like on Home) are drastically oversized, breaking the calm hierarchy.

spacing.note: Good use of a consistent grid, though some internal card paddings feel slightly tight compared to Vercel standards.

states.note: Loading states are present, but empty states (like 'No live report') lack the polished illustration/layout of top-tier apps.

hierarchy.note: Strong visual separation of primary and secondary content, especially in the dense right-hand trace sidebars.

interaction.note: Excellent visibility of keyboard shortcuts. Hover states are implied but list views currently show too many default actions.

craft.note: Subtle borders and consistent radiuses are well executed. Gradient cards in Reports are the only major outlier.

opportunities.opportunity: Scale down the massive H1 headline on the Home view.
opportunities.why: The 'One useful thing...' headline is disproportionately large compared to the rest of the dense, power-user UI, breaking the 'dense-but-calm' aesthetic. Notion and Vercel cap page titles around 28-32px to maintain focus on the data.
opportunities.fixHint: Reduce font-size to 28px or 32px, set line-height to 1.2, and use a semibold weight (600) instead of black/extrabold.
opportunities.verify: The headline should feel like a page title, not a marketing landing page hero.

opportunities.opportunity: Hide secondary actions in Inbox rows behind a hover state.
opportunities.why: Currently, every row shows 3-4 buttons (Re-run, Open, Snooze, Dismiss). This creates massive visual clutter. Linear keeps lists clean by revealing actions only when the user hovers over the specific row.
opportunities.fixHint: Keep the primary action (e.g., 'Open DISCO') visible or implied by clicking the row. Move 'Snooze' and 'Dismiss' to an opacity: 0 state that transitions to opacity: 1 on row :hover.
opportunities.verify: The inbox should look significantly cleaner and less overwhelming at first glance.

opportunities.opportunity: Replace heavy gradient backgrounds on Report cards with subtle borders/accents.
opportunities.why: The heavy, multi-colored gradients (blue, orange, purple) clash with the otherwise restrained, neutral Vercel-like palette. They draw too much attention away from the content.
opportunities.fixHint: Use a solid white background with a standard 1px gray-200 border. Indicate the 'type' or 'status' with a subtle 2px top border accent color or a small colored dot next to the title.
opportunities.verify: The Reports grid should feel cohesive with the rest of the application's minimalist styling.

opportunities.opportunity: Replace text-heavy status badges with color-coded dots.
opportunities.why: Badges like 'verified' and 'needs review' inside the gradient headers add unnecessary reading overhead. Linear uses simple colored dots (green, amber, red) to convey status instantly without clutter.
opportunities.fixHint: Replace the pill badges with a 6px or 8px border-radius dot (e.g., bg-green-500 for verified) placed next to the report title, with a native title attribute for hover context.
opportunities.verify: Status should be scannable via color without needing to read the text in the badge.

opportunities.opportunity: Refine the 'No live report halo yet' empty state.
opportunities.why: The current empty state is a simple dashed box with text. Vercel empty states use a subtle, monochromatic icon, concise copy, and a clear primary CTA to make empty areas feel intentional rather than broken.
opportunities.fixHint: Center the content. Add a muted 24px icon (like a document or spark) above the text. Make the 'Create first packet' button a standard primary button rather than a full-width outline button.
opportunities.verify: The empty state should look like a deliberate onboarding step rather than a placeholder.
